statement: You are given a positive integer base x and a non-negative integer exponent n. Return xⁿ.

Multiplying x by itself n times takes n steps. Binary exponentiation takes O(log n): look at the bits of n from lowest to highest, squaring the base at each step and multiplying it into the result whenever the current bit of n is 1. This works because xⁿ is the product of x^(2ᵏ) over the bits k that are set in n.
This is the integer form of the problem. The LeetCode version also allows a fractional base and a negative exponent.

examples.explanation: 10 is 1010 in binary, so 2¹⁰ = 2⁸ × 2². The squares 2, 4, 16, 256 are formed, and the ones for bits 1 and 3 (4 and 256) are multiplied together to give 1024.
Any base raised to the power 0 is 1. The exponent has no set bits, so the result keeps its starting value of 1.
